Another very active week for Bulk carriers with numerous vessels changing hands and transactions taking place across all segments. Despite the small decline of the BDI since the start of the week, we do not interpret this as a signal for Buyers to pause their acquisition efforts. On the contrary, we expect purchasing activity to remain robust, as an increasing number of enquiries continue to emerge. Starting with the Newcastlemax sector, following their recent sale of three units to UAE based buyers, Messrs '2020 Bulkers' have now offloaded another vessel from their modern fleet, namely the **BULK SAO PAULO** (ABT 208K DWT, 2020, NEW TIMES, SCRUBBER) which has achieved a price of USD 72.25m from Belgian Buyers. The Capesize segment remains very active as well, with the **ROSEMARY** (ABT 179K DWT, 2010 DSME), which was inviting offers on the 21<sup>st</sup> of October, getting tied up at levels of around USD 28.5m, while the one year younger CMB-owned **MINERAL SUBIC** (ABT 179K DWT, 2011 HANJIN SUBIC) has managed to achieve levels of low USD 30m from Chinese interests. On the older tonnage, Mssrs 'Seacon' have emerged as the Buyers of a 2006 blt unit owned in China, the **AP POWER** (ABT 173K DWT, 2006 BOHAI), which has achieved levels of mid USD 14m. Less activity has been taking place on the Kamsarmax sector, with the most notable sale of the week being the **FJELD SAGA** (ABT 83K DWT, 2013, SANOYAS) which changed hands for a price of circa USD 20m from Messrs 'ADS', marking their return in ship-owning. Geared tonnage remained in demand, with one sale on the Supramax front, the **INCE EGE** (ABT 57K DWT, 2010, STX DALIAN) which has managed to achieve a price of high USD 12m from u/d buyers, basis surveys freshly passed and with the majority of this week's sales being Handysize tonnage. The most notable was the Japanese controlled **OCEAN TACT** (ABT 36K DWT, 2019, SHIKOKU, SCRUBBER) which has been committed at an unconfirmed price, as reports have emerged that she achieved USD 24 m, however others following the Vessel believe she has achieved levels in the 23's. Furthermore, the **VEGA FALKTIND** (ABT 32K DWT, 2011 FUJIAN MAWEI) has been committed to u/d interests for levels in the mid USD 8m while the one-year-younger **ARAWANA** (ABT 32K DWT, 2012, TAIZHOU MAPLE LEAF) is now committed for u/d levels, about three weeks after the sale of the sister-ship from the same Owners the NEPTUNE, which had managed to achieve levels of USD 9m at the time. Finally, one more smaller Handysize has been sold to Vietnamese buyers, the **DANSHIP BULKER** (ABT 28K DWT, 2009, I-S) for a price of USD 8.5m.

Although this has been another busy week for tankers, there are only a couple of sales to report, with the most interesting one being the sale of the 'Thenamaris' owned Suezmax tanker **SEAVOYAGER** (**ABT 159K DWT, 2007, HYUNDAI**) which is changing hands for levels of rgn USD 37.2m. Buyers are believed to be Chinese. On the smaller sizes, another MR tanker, the **JAG POOJA** (ABT 48K DWT, 2005, IWAGI) has been sold, achieving levels of USD 11.5m from undisclosed interests.

Another 15-year-old Capesize has changed hands this week, highlighting the continued strong demand for vessels of this vintage over the last couple of months. The **mv Rosemary** (abt 179k dwt, built 2010 Daewoo) was inviting offers earlier this month and, following healthy competition with more than ten bids received, has now been sold for around USD 28.5m. In the geared segment, a couple of Supramax sales were concluded. The Japanese-controlled **mv** **Atacama Queen** (abt 5k dwt, built 2011 Imabari, **OHBH**) has been sold at USD 14.5m while the older **mv** **Evriali** (abt 53k dwt, built 2007 Iwagi) has changed hands at USD 10.3m, with dry dock due promptly in November.

A comparatively quiet week on the tankers with no confirmed sales reported. However, market rumors indicate a 20-year-old Suezmax having been committed for a price in the mid USD 29 m's range. It will be interesting to observe price levels in the coming weeks, particularly for crude carriers, as sentiment remains firm amid the ongoing strength in the chartering market.

S&P activity has remained steady and continued at the same pace this week, with a solid flow of transactions taking place and no immediate indications that such conditions are likely to shift any time soon. Demand for dry cargo bulkers and particularly high-quality units built at reputable shipyards, remains strong. On the larger sizes, the Imabari built **SEACON AFRICA** (ABT 206K DWT, 2006, IMABARI) was sold at USD 22.7 m to Chinese buyers, whilst on Panamaxes, the **ORNAK** (ABT 79K DWT, 2010, NEW CENTURY) which invited offers on the 27<sup>th</sup> of Oct, has been sold achieving levels in the Low 11's m. Most activity this week was centered around geared vessels, with the most notable sale in the Ultramaxes being the **CMB BRUEGEL** (ABT 63K DWT, 2021, SHIN KASADO) which has been sold to Meghna Group, Bangladesh for a price in the region of USD 33 m basis delivery in Q1 2026 with surveys freshly passed. On Supramaxes, the **INCE FORTUNE** (ABT 57K DWT, 2010, STX DALIAN) has achieved a price in the Mid-to-High USD 12's m levels, whilst the **KARADENIZ S** (ABT 57K DWT, 2012, STX SB KOREA) is committed at levels slightly in excess of USD 14 m to Turkish interests. On Handies, the **YANGTZE FLOURISH** (ABT 32K DWT, 2012, JIANGMEN NANYANG) has been sold for a price in the High USD 9's m to Chinese buyers.

It has been a rather active week in terms of on-going discussions taking place in the products and crude sectors. Most notable sales are the 4x 2014 HMD built Scrubber fitted MR's (namely **STI BATTERY**, **STI VENERE**, **STI MILWAUKEE**, and **STI YORKVILLE**) that Scorpio Tankers has sold for region USD 128 m enbloc i.e. USD 32 m per vessel, basis delivery during Q1 2026. At the same time, Scorpio Tankers announced it agreed to purchase **4x scrubber fitted MR Newbuildings**, currently under construction at Jingjiang Nanyang Shipbuilding, China at a purchase price of USD 45 m per vessel and with expected deliveries 2Q-3Q 2026 and 1Q-2Q 2027.

With Bahri Week in Dubai underway, the S&P market has seen the anticipated slowdown in activity. Only a limited number of transactions have been concluded, notably the following: On the Handymax segment, the **YANGTZE NOVA** (abt 47k dwt, built 2013, Jiangsu Eastern) sold for a price in the region of USD 12m, and the Handysize, the **EMIL SELMER** (abt 32k dwt, built 2010, Jiangsu Zhenjiang) has also been sold at range USD 8m basis surveys due and prompt delivery in China.

Similar pattern on the wet side as well, where UAE-based buyers acquired this week a couple of pumproom-type MR2s from Maersk Tankers. Specifically, the **MAERSK MISSISSIPPI** and the **MAERSK MARU** (abt 48k dwt, built 2011 and 2010 Iwagi) changed hands for USD 44m enbloc. For comparison, a couple of weeks ago the 2011-built sistership **YOSEMITE TRADER** was reported sold for around USD 21.5m, basis SS/DD due in March 2026.

Following the slower activity during Bahri Week in Dubai, the S&P market has gained traction, especially in the dry segment. Several transactions have been concluded, with the below being the most notable ones. To begin with, on the larger sizes, the Mini-cape **NBA REMBRANDT** (ABT 107KDWT, 2012, OSHIMA) was sold for a price of USD 18.7 mill., to clients of GCL Shipping. Furthermore, on the Panamax sector, a new sale of a Japanese vessel has emerged, the **YASA UNITY** (ABT 75KDWT, 2006, SANOYAS HISHINO), which was reported sold to undisclosed buyers at low USD 9 mill., while, on the Ultramax sector, the **SANTA MARIA** (ABT 61KDWT, 2014, IWAGI ZOSEN) achieved levels of low USD 21 mill. basis forward delivery in June 2026. Finally, the Handysize sector seems to remain the one with the most activity, as we have noticed three transactions that have taken place. The **SATURNIA** (ABT 38KDWT, 2015, JIANGMEN NANYANG) was acquired by Pioneer Marine for USD 18.5 mill. The **FEDERAL YELLOWSTONE** (ABT 37KDWT, 2013, ZHEJIANG YANGFAN) has been committed to Greek interests for levels of high USD 14 mill. and, lastly, one more - slightly smaller- Handysize, the **YANGTZE GRACE** (ABT 32KDWT, 2012, JIANGMEN NANYANG) has been reported sold for high USD 9 mill to Chinese buyers.

On the tankers, the most significant transaction has been the resale of the two Atlas' Suezmaxes delivering ex Daehan, S. Korea in January 2026, the **VIKING STAR & NORTH STAR** (ABT 159K DWT, DAEHAN, DELY 1/2026), for a price of USD 97 m. each to Okeanis Eco Tankers. On the older tonnage, 2 x Korean blt MR tankers **PS QUEEN & PS DREAM** (ABT 51KDWT, 2006, STX) have been sold enbloc for levels slightly below USD 28 mill. to Indian buyers.

S&P market remained active this week, maintaining its recent momentum and asset values remaining firm. On the larger size, Capes continue to attract firm prices, attributed to the lack of quality candidates in combination with the positive expectations & outlook in this sector. The Imabari built **FORTUNE VIOLET** (ABT 181K DWT, 2012, IMABARI) was sold at USD 34 m to undisclosed buyers, whilst we understand a one-year older Japanese built Capesize has been sold in the region of USD 32 m. On Ultramaxes, the most notable transaction of the week was the resale of the 2x Jaldhi Overseas Ultramaxes **JAL KANAK & JAL KUNDAN** (ABT 66K DWT, 2026, YANGZI-MITSUI) at USD 37.25 m. On Supramaxes, the **JIN SUI** (ABT 56K DWT, 2008, SHANGHAI SHIPYARD) was acquired by Forever Win Shipping for a price of USD 10.3 m, whilst the **VEGA STETIND** (ABT 55K DWT, 2008, OSHIMA) changed hands for levels in the low USD 11's m to Chinese interests. Lastly, the **INTREPID** (ABT 52K DWT, 2005, TSUNEISHI CEBU) was also acquired by Chinese buyers in the low USD 10 m. Meantime we await to see final levels achieved for a couple of Kamsarmaxes that were inviting offers this week, namely the **KEY FRONTIER** (ABT 80K DWT, 2011, UNIVERSAL JAPAN) and the **BW MATSUYAMA** (ABT 82K DWT, 2019, TSUNEISHI CEBU), for which we will be able to report more accurately next week.

Whilst demand for tankers remains robust and especially for the larger size eco-type crude oil tankers, it has been a rather slower week in terms of confirmed sales, with the only reported sale being the **SAPPHIRA** (ABT 149K DWT, 2008, UNIVERSAL SB), sold at a price in the region of USD 37 m to undisclosed buyers.

As the year draws to a close, activity slowed during the first week of December in both the dry and the wet sectors. In the Kamsarmax segment, following last week's invitation for offers, the **KEY FRONTIER** (ABT 80K DWT, 2011, UNIVERSAL SB MAIZURU) has been acquired by Greek interest at USD 18.7 m. Meanwhile, the **BW MATSUYAMA** (ABT 81K DWT, 2019, TSUNEISHI CEBU) remains under negotiations. Within the Supramax sector, two additional sales were recorded. The **JIN BI** (ABT 56K DWT, 2012, JIANGSU NEW HANTONG, electronic main engine) was confirmed sold to Xing Le Investments, Hong Kong at USD 14.4 m, while the **INCE KASTAMONU** (ABT 56K DWT, 2010, COSCO ZHOUSHAN) changed hands to undisclosed buyers at USD 12.8 m. Overall, the Supramax market has shown firming sentiment in recent months, with asset values trending upward compared to the summer period, when a 2012 Chinese built 56K DWT vessel achieved a price of USD 13.25 m, while a 2010 Chinese built 58K DWT was sold at USD 11.2 m. The Ultramax **IVS WINDSOR** (ABT 60K DWT, 2016, OSHIMA SB) invited offers this week and we are waiting to see the outcome, which we will be able to report further next week.
Another relatively slower week on the tanker market, with no confirmed sales reported.

With the Christmas holidays drawing near and the freight market easing, S&P activity has slowed down, as many prospective buyers are postponing their purchasing plans until the new year. Nonetheless, there remains a healthy buying appetite with main culprits still being Chinese buyers for the older tonnage, whilst enquiry for the younger, and especially eco type tonnage, coming from the West. The standout sale of the week was the Newcastlemax **ATLANTIC LION** (ABT 210K DWT, 2020, SWS, SCRUBBER), with surveys freshly passed, which was reported sold to Korean interests at USD 73.75 m. The last comparable transaction is the enbloc sale of the 2 Newcastlemax vessels **BULK SANTOS / BULK SYDNEY** (ABT 208K DWT, 2020, NEW TIMES) at a total price of USD 145.5 m (USD 72.75 m each). On Kamsarmaxes, we are hearing unconfirmed rumors of a 2021 Kamsarmax built at a Japanese-affiliated yard, being committed in the high USD 33's m levels. Whilst on the Ultramax segment, following last week's invitation for offers, Oceanstar Management have now secured the eco type **IVS WINDSOR** (ABT 60k DWT, 2016, OSHIMA) at a price in the low/mid USD 25 m range.

Meanwhile, on the tanker front, all eyes are on the two VLCCs **TWIN POLLUX / TWIN CASTOR** (ABT 320K DWT, 2014/2013, BOHAI), which invited offers this week. The outcome of the process is expected to provide valuable insight into current appetite for modern large crude tonnage. We expect clarity to emerge shortly and look forward to providing an update in next week's report.

As we move through the end of Q4, we see a seasonal uptick in transactions across several segments. Chinese buyers are accelerating acquisitions ahead of the Lunar New Year, aiming to secure coverage during the upcoming holiday period, especially on larger ships. We are hearing several 15-year-old Capes are being negotiated to Chinese buyers, and we expect to be able to report further on this next week. On the geared sector, we note the sale of the Supramax **WARIYA NAREE** (ABT 53K DWT, 2011, HINUSTAN) reported sold at USD 9.85 m. To compare, her one-year older sister vessel **WARISA NAREE** (ABT 53K DWT, 2010, HINDUSTAN), with better surveys position, changed hands last month at USD 9.5 m. Furthermore, the OHBS Supramax **SUN MASTER** (ABT 50K DWT, 2011, OSHIMA) invited offers and we understand that have attracted interest from several parties, reflecting healthy appetite for Japanese built mid-age tonnage. In addition, the larger Supramax **CLARA** (ABT 56K DWT, 2008, I.H.I. YOKOHAMA) has also invited offers this week, and we expect to be able to report on the outcome shortly.

On the wet side, there is a lot of Chinese demand for 20-year-old VLCCs, but available tonnage remains limited. In the LR2 space, c/o Scorpio Tankers reportedly sold their **STI GALLANTRY & STI GOAL** (ABT 109K DWT, 2016, GUANGZHOU NANSHA) for USD 52.3 m each, replacing them with two scrubber-fitted LR2 newbuildings at Dalian Shipbuilding, for USD 70.8 m each basis Q3 2027 delivery. On the MR sector, the **NORD SUPERIOR** (ABT 49K DWT, 2015, STX JINHAE) has changed hands to Chinese interest in the region of USD 33.75 m.

Following the start of the year, we see continuous activity on both dry and tanker markets. The dry cargo market has held up with a steady flow of transactions, while the tanker sector has seen particularly strong momentum, driven by significant VLCC deals that have set a confident tone for the opening weeks of the year.

In the larger segment, we are hearing rumors of a 2011 Japanese built Capesize being committed at levels of USD 32.5 m net, while at the Kamsarmax front, the **CENTURY SHANGHAI** (ABT 81K DWT, 2018, CHENGXI) has been sold via auction for USD 25.02 m. In the Ultramax segment, the **STARRY NIGHT** (ABT 61K DWT, 2022, NANTONG COSCO) achieved a price of USD 32.5 m, basis March – April delivery. Furthermore, another auction sale has been concluded, with the Supramax **JIANG YUAN NAN JING** (ABT 50K DWT, 2003, NACKS) achieving levels of USD 7.54 m. In the Handysize sector, the **FETHIYE-M** (ABT 37K DWT, 2011, SPP GOSEONG) has now been sold to Greek interests in the high USD 12 m, while the **BULKER BEE 30** (ABT 34K DWT, 2010, TK) has been sold at USD 11.3 m. Finally, we are hearing of a 2016 Tsuneishi Cebu built Handysize being committed for levels of USD 19.1 m.

The key transaction of the week involved c/o Frontline selling 8 x VLCCs (2015-2016 built - 1<sup>st</sup> generation ECO m/e) for an aggregate value of USD 831.5 m, with deliveries scheduled during Q1 2026. In parallel, the owners have agreed to acquire 9 x Newbuilding VLCCs with scrubbers for the amount of USD 1.224 bn, with deliveries running from Q3 2026 throughout Q2 2027. In addition, c/o CMB.TECH have sold 6 x VLCCs (2007-2016 built) enbloc, with deliveries also scheduled for Q1 2026, generating an estimated capital gain of around USD 261 m.

After the significant S&P activity observed last week, especially driven by the VLCC segment, the wet market remains highly active, with substantial movement observed across all segments. On the dry side, although there has been some softening on rates, S&P demand remains present and acquisitions continue to emerge, with buyers adopting a cautious but opportunistic approach.

This week, dry bulk activity was concentrated in the larger segments, where c/o Berge Bulk sold their scrubber-fitted Newcastlemax **BERGE MOLDOVEANU** (ABT 211K DWT, 2020, BOHAI, SCRUBBER), for a price in the region of USD 74 m to Korean interests. Furthermore, we are hearing of two Capesize units being sold this week, the **FRONTIER KOTOBUKI** (174K DWT, 2011, NAMURA) which was inviting offers yesterday, we understand that has been committed for USD 31 m, and another vintage unit which is built in Japan 2005 at a price of USD 20.5 m. In the geared segment, the Ultramax **OCEAN JASMIN** (ABT 63K DWT, 2019, COSCO HI ZHOUSHAN) has been sold in the region of USD 28.5 m basis TC attached until max June 2026. Unconfirmed rumors suggest two Ultramax transactions being concluded, including a 2012 Japanese built unit at a price in the low USD 19 m and a 2020 Chinese built vessel, said to be sold for xs USD 30 m. On the smaller segment, c/o Straits Orient Lines sold their Handysize **TBC PRAISE** (ABT 36K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI MIPO) for USD 14.4 m, while on the Chinese built front, we understand that a 37K DWT, 2012 unit is being negotiated in the levels of low/mid USD 11 m.

The tanker sector has remained busy, VLCC transactions continued to unfold, while demand remains notably strong throughout different sizes, reflecting sustained buyer interest and confident sentiment. On the LR segment, c/o Scorpio Tankers have sold their scrubber-fitted LR2 **STI KINGSWAY** (ABT 109K DWT, 2015, SUNGDONG, SCRUBBER) at USD 57.5 m to undisclosed buyers. Meanwhile, on the MRs, the two zinc-coated eco-MR tankers **MARITIME TRANQUILITY & MARITIME COMITY** (ABT 49K DWT, 2020, GSI NANSHA) have been reported sold to Greek interests for USD 39 m each.

Another active week on the tanker front, with a steady flow of transactions and ongoing negotiations taking place across all vessel segments. On the dry side, interest remains high with several new sales emerging as market sentiment strengthens.

On the Kamsarmax front, the **MIAO XIANG** (ABT 81K DWT, 2013, JIANGSU EASTERN) has been sold at USD 16.8 m, while on the Panamax segment, the **KT BIRDIE** (ABT 74K DWT, 2011, SASEBO HI) changed hands at USD 16.5 m to Greek interests. We are also hearing that a 2020 Chinese built Ultramax has been sold for USD 30.1 m. Meanwhile, **THE LOVING** (ABT 58K DWT, 2007, TSUNEISHI CEBU) has been committed at USD 11.7 m. On the Handysize segment, we are seeing several transactions unfolding and negotiations taking place, highlighting also buyers' appetite for smaller tonnage. The **YANGTZE GRACE & YANGTZE HAPPINESS** (ABT 32K DWT, 2012, JIANGMEN NANYANG) were sold for USD 9.8 m each to separate Chinese interests. According to market rumors a 37K DWT 2008 Japanese built Handysize has been sold for USD 11.4 m, whilst a 2015 Japanese built 36K DWT Handysize is in firm discussions in the high USD 18's m.

On the Suezmax segment, c/o Okeanis have agreed to acquire two resale Suezmaxes currently under construction at Daehan Shipbuilding at a price of USD 99.3 m per vessel with delivery within the second quarter of 2026. Meanwhile, we are hearing a 2009 Chinese built Suezmax has been sold at USD 42.5 m. Lastly, two modern LR2s 109K DWT 2024 built are rumored sold at USD 84.5 m each.

Compared to previous weeks, the dry bulk market has shown increased strength. The gearless tonnage led the way with few mid aged KMXs and PMXs being sold. On the wet side, following an exceptionally strong start of the year, sales activity moderated. However, overall sentiment remains constructive, supported by continued interest especially in the crude sector.

On the gearless segment a couple of Kamsarmaxes have been sold. The **RIZE** (ABT 81K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI MIPO) at circa USD 17.5m, and a 20-year-old Japanese built ship that, according to rumors, has achieved levels in the high USD 10'sm. On the Panamax front, the **GLOBAL BONANZA** (ABT 75K DWT, 2011, SASEBO) sold at USD 15.3 m to Greek interests, basis surveys due. We are hearing that a 2006 LME has also been sold for USD 9.7m. Meanwhile, the Ultramax **MITSOS** (ABT 63K DWT, 2013, CHENGXI) was acquired by Greek interests for USD 20.5m.

Following the numerous VLCCs sales of the past few weeks, another vintage ship has been reported sold, namely the **DHT BAUHINIA** (ABT 301K DWT, 2007, DAEWOO) that fetched a price of USD 51.5m basis June-July delivery.

Snp markets have maintained strong sentiment across sectors, building on a positive start to the year. On the dry bulk side, the prevailing trend continues to favor larger tonnage transactions, supported by firm freight rates despite the approaching Lunar New Year, a period that is traditionally slower for market activity. Meanwhile, the tanker market has recorded another strong week, with demand continuing to build rapidly and buyer appetite remaining robust. Numerous discussions are currently underway, and we are expecting to be able to report more sales in the coming weeks.

On the bulk carrier front, several transactions occurred across a wide range of sizes. At the larger end, the Capesize **ROBUSTO** (ABT 174 DWT, 2006, SWS, SCRUBBER) was sold to Chinese interests for USD 19.5 m with delivery in Far East between April – May 2026. In the Post Panamax segment, the **JP CARETTA** (ABT 88K DWT, 2008, IMABARI, SCRUBBER) was reported sold at region USD 13 m, while the Kamsarmax **GASTONE** (ABT 81K DWT, 2012, SUNGDONG) achieved a price of USD 17.6 m. Within the geared segment, the Supramax **SPAR CANIS** (ABT 53K DWT, 2006, SHANGHAI CHENGXI) was reported sold at region USD 9 m to Chinese buyers, and the Handysize **JETSTREAM** (ABT 34K, 2012, SPP GOSEONG) changed hands at USD 13.5 m.
On the tanker sector, the LR1 **ATHIRI** (ABT 74K DWT, 2010, SPP SACHEON) was acquired by Greek interests at USD 25 m.

On the dry side, Chinese interests have been particularly active in the Capesize segment. Meanwhile, the tanker market maintains solid momentum across all sectors, with strong buying appetite from Far Eastern and Greek buyers.

On the Capesize front, activity has remained firm, with several notable transactions concluded during the week. The scrubber-fitted **STAR SCARLETT** (ABT 175K DWT, 2014, JINHAI, SCRUBBER) was acquired by Chinese interests at around USD 36 m. Meantime, the **EPIC** (ABT 182K DWT, 2010, ODENSE LINDO) was sold at USD 32.5 m, and the same aged Chinese built **CAPE BRAZIL** (ABT 177K DWT, 2010, SWS) achieved a price of USD 31 m. In the Handysize segment, activity was more selective, yet present. The **CS CANDY** (ABT 37K DWT, 2012, TIANJIN XIANGANG, ICE CLASS 1C) was sold at levels in the mid to high USD 11s m.

On tankers, the VLCC sector witnessed another landmark transaction, as c/o Pan Ocean secured 10 scrubber-fitted VLCCs from SK Shipping, including units built between 2008 and 2013. The enbloc deal concluded at around USD 668 m and includes attached time-charter agreements back to SK Shipping. C/o Euronav have sold the sister VLCCs **ILMA & INGRID** (ABT 318K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI HI) to S. Korean interests reportedly generating a combined capital gain of USD 98.2 m. The transaction highlights the strong demand and continued liquidity in the VLCC space, with a stronger preference towards Korean-built tonnage. Meanwhile on Suezmaxes, c/o Nordic Tankers sold the **NORDIC POLLUX** (ABT 150K DWT, 2003, NKK (TSU)) at USD 25 m. The product tanker segment has also been experiencing increased activity. On MRs, the **UOG OSLO** (ABT 46K DWT, 2010, HYUNDAI MIPO) was sold at USD 23.5 m, and the sisters **ELANDRA FJORD & ELANDRA BALTIC** (ABT 51K DWT, 2011, HYUNDAI MIPO) achieved USD 24.5 m each from Greek interests.

Activity has moderated this week as the Lunar New Year period temporarily slows market momentum. But despite seasonal slowdown, overall asset values continue to hold at firm levels across sectors, reflecting underlying confidence in earnings and sustained buying appetite. With several offer deadlines scheduled for next week, activity is expected to accelerate, and we will be able to report further as the market momentum builds.

Further activity was recorded in the larger sizes, with the Capesize **MICHALIS H** (ABT 180K DWT, 2012, DAILAN, SCRUBBER) reported sold at USD 35.2 m, reflecting continued appetite for Capesize tonnage. In the geared segment, the Supramax **LIANSON DYNAMIC** (ABT 53K DWT, 2006, CHENGXI) was reported sold at levels in xs USD 9 m. Whilst we are hearing of a 2010 Japanese built Supramax being committed in levels close to USD 15 m.

On the VLCC front, the scrubber fitted **SINGAPORE SPIRIT** (ABT 318K DWT, 2013, SWS) is reported sold at USD 84.5 m to C/O Sinokor. Additionally, on the Aframax segment, the Korean built **P. SOPHIA** (ABT 105K DWT, 2009, Hyundai HI Ulsan) has changed hands achieving USD 36.65 m. Meanwhile, in the MR space, the zinc coated **CABO NEGRO II** (ABT 47K DWT, 2006, SK Onishi) is reported sold at levels in the low USD 14 m range.

Both dry bulk and tanker secondhand markets have remained active, with bulker deals particularly active. Transactions continue to materialize, reflecting sustained buyer appetite despite asset prices across both sectors continuing to hold at strong levels, supporting overall market confidence.

On the Kamsarmax front, c/o Agricore Shipping have concluded the sale of the **ASL MOON** (ABT 81K DWT, 2008, MITSUI TAMANO) at USD 13.6 m to Chinese interests, basis surveys due September 2026. Meanwhile, after having invited offers earlier in the week, the **THREE SASKIAS** (ABT 80K DWT, 2014, JMU TSU) has been reported sold at USD 26.7 m to Chinese interests. **GIEWONT** (ABT 79K DWT, 2010, NEW CENTURY) has been concluded at USD 11.8 m, with Chinese buyers understood behind the deal. In the Supramax segment, c/o Densay Shipping have sold the **SSI ERDOGAN BEY** (ABT 50K DWT, 2010, OSHIMA) at USD 15 m, basis surveys freshly passed. Finally, in the Handysize sector, the **ADVENTURE** (ABT 33K DWT, 2011, WEIHAI SAMJIN) has changed hands at USD 9.5 m.

The scrubber fitted Suezmax **SIGRUN** (ABT 156K DWT, 2013, SUMITOMO) is reported sold at USD 65 m to C/O Naftomar. Additionally, In the MR space, the scrubber-fitted sister vessels **NORD MAVERICK** and **NORD MARVEL** (ABT 50,000 DWT, 2020, HMD) are understood to be sold enbloc at levels in excess of USD 90 million to undisclosed buyers.

Asset prices, particularly in the Tanker sector, have seen a remarkable upswing following the sharp spike in freight rates triggered by the developments in the Middle East. We are also noticing strong competition on the Dry side, mainly for Japanese built tonnage, with some vessels being offered for sale managing to attract more than a dozen buyers.

The Capesize **CAPE SANDRA** (ABT 175K DWT, 2011, HHIC-SUBIC) has been reported sold at region USD 32 m, basis surveys due in May 2026. On the Panamax front, c/o Evalend have concluded the sale of the sister-vessels **TRINITY I & ROZA** (ABT 93K DWT, 2010, JIANGSU NEW YANGZIJIAN) for an enbloc price in the region of USD 23 m. What a week! One of the biggest and busiest Posidonia events ever. With the majority of shipping sectors enjoying healthy market conditions, the global maritime community gathered in Athens for a week of meetings, networking, celebrations, and strategic discussions. The overall sentiment was positive, with market participants expressing optimism that supportive fundamentals will continue to underpin freight markets in the months ahead. At the same time, there remains a degree of caution regarding ongoing geopolitical developments in the Middle East and their potential implications for global trade flows, energy markets, and overall economic stability. S&P demand and activity remain robust, with the shortage of modern eco-design bulkers and tankers still very evident. One might have expected more owners to take advantage of current asset values and bring additional tonnage to the market; however, many continue to prefer retaining exposure to what they believe could be a prolonged period of healthy earnings. Looking ahead, the industry appears to be entering the second half of the year with a constructive outlook. While macroeconomic and geopolitical risks cannot be ignored, the prevailing mood at Posidonia suggested that most market participants remain confident in the resilience of shipping markets and the opportunities that lie ahead.

Although no new tanker sales can be reported, several negotiations are understood to be ongoing this week.

As many had anticipated, the U.S.-Iran ceasefire has failed to hold, with renewed hostilities threatening to undermine the fragile optimism that the traffic in the Straits of Hormuz will be fully restored sooner than later. The latest developments have reinforced concerns that geopolitical risks remain elevated and continue to influence the decisions of Buyers and Sellers in all segments. On the commodity side, coal demand in the Far East is expected to strengthen, with Vietnam projected to reach record coal imports in 2026. This growth is driven by government plans to expand the country's power generation capacity through alternative energy sources, including coal. More broadly, this reflects a trend that other energy-import-dependent countries may also follow if tensions in the Middle East persist and continue to disrupt global energy supply routes, suggesting an optimistic landscape for seaborne trade in the short-and-medium-term. These developments have been reflected in this week's Drybulk market, where Capesize experienced a strong week, with the Baltic Capesize Index closing today at 4,655, representing a 13.5% week-on-week increase. In Tankers, VLCC activity in the Middle East has strengthened as well, further bolstered by Saudi Aramco's aggressive price cuts for its August crude export program and the UAE's record-high crude oil production in June following its exit from the OPEC. Fixture volumes have increased as a result, although it remains uncertain whether fixtures from inside the Strait of Hormuz will conclude.

Activity in the Ultramax market saw the **HAATO** (ABT 61,472 DWT, 2011, SHIN KASADO DOCK, C:4X30.5T) committed to C/O ADNOC at USD 23.5m, with the deal concluded basis freshly passed surveys. Elsewhere, in the Supramax sector **EVEREST** (ABT 57,480 DWT, 2012, STX SB (JINHAE), C:4X30T) reportedly sold for a price in the low USD 16m's. Additionally, the modern Handysize **JNS PHOENIX** (ABT 40,552 DWT, 2025 JIANGMEN NANYANG, C:4X30T) has been committed at a price of excess USD 34m after calling for offers. Further down the size spectrum the **HTK LUCKY** (ABT 28,481 DWT, 2003 IMABARI SB (IMABARI), C:4X30.5T) changed hands, with the transaction agreed at around USD 6m.
Although we understand several negotiations to be ongoing, there are no new tanker sales to report this week.

Events in the Middle East are continuing to shape shipping dynamics. With disruptions now affecting Saudi Arabia's two key export routes—the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb—the effective voyage duration for Middle Eastern crude destined for Asia has increased by approximately one month and tanker earnings have now climbed at a weighted average of USD 75,000/ day, highest number since early May. Market outlook appears to be overall positive, supported by fundamentals such as the continued growth in long-haul exports, increasing Venezuelan exports now carried on “mainstream” tankers, and oil restocking margins. S&P tanker activity was further bolstered this week, with several fairly modern VLCCs understood to have been transacted to Middle Eastern interests at firm price levels, supporting sentiment across the rest of the tanker market. We also understand that several eco MR2s ranging from circa 10-year-old units up to resales are currently under firm negotiations. Furthermore, buying appetite continues to extend also on the older units, within the 15–20-year-old range – in which we still monitor a number of buyers, mostly from the Middle East and Far East markets, being on the look-out for MRs & LR1s as well as crude takers, more specifically on Aframaxes & Suezmaxes. Dry market has held to a robust first half of the year, underpinned by strong iron ore exports from Australia and Brazil, alongside resilient Chinese import demand despite elevated inventories and softer domestic steel production. Additional support has come from steady minor bulk trade and healthy Atlantic grain export volumes. Looking ahead, the Capesize segment is expected to continue outperforming the smaller size classes, driven by sustained growth in long-haul Atlantic iron ore exports and favorable ton-mile demand. In terms of activity, market sources indicated a number of approximately 15-year-old Korean- and Japanese-built Kamsarmax units as being currently in advanced negotiations, while the focus of Dry Tonnage buyers seems to be in the 15-20-years-old Supramax-Ultramax segment, driven by Far Eastern market players
